EN: When hovering over a part in the parts toolbox you will see the details of that part in the popup window. \nYou can adjust how much detail is shown by right-clicking the icon in the toolbox. Right-clicking can also \npin the window so you can scroll the longer information boxes.
Module Details: This section contains more details on the specific modules that make up the part.
General Details:\nBasic information like mass, resource \ncapacity, crew capacity and more.
Description:\nLearn a bit more about the use \nand history of each part.
Part Name and Model:\nIncluding a one meter scale for \nreference.
Cost:\nMonitoring your build costs \nin career mode is key.

Part Picker: Left-click to pick up parts from the toolbox and use them in the editor. You can also drop unwanted parts here to discard them. Part Details: Right-click the part in the toolbox to toggle the display of additional info.
Advanced Mode:\nWith advanced mode enabled you can right-click multiple filter categories to apply an "and" filter, e.g. to \nselect all Mk2 parts that have Liquid Fuel resource.
Toggle Advanced Mode: Click this to show/hide the additional advanced filters including resource type, bulkhead size, tech level and more.
Sort Actions: Hopefully this is self-explanatory... if not, left-click a label to sort the parts.
You will find the items you need to build a vessel in the parts toolbox. Through the use of filters you can \ntarget a search for that perfect part.
Custom Categories: You can make custom groupings of parts here for your favorite styles.
Sub Assemblies:\nUse this to store assemblies of \nparts for reuse on later vessels.

There are two types of symmetry - radial and mirror. Radial symmetry is usually used with rockets to \nplace 2, 3, 4 or more parts around the central axis. Mirror symmetry is what you normally use with \naircraft to place items either side of the center line.

The angle snap tool makes it easier to get exact angles around \nthe centerline of the vessel. By default it works in 15° increments; \nholding down                 will make it to work in finer 5° steps.
To help balance your vessels when building, there are two functions that can be a great help.
The vessel details panel lets you \nset the name and description for \nthe current vessel.
The scene action buttons give you control over what happens to your vessel.
New Vessel:\nClean the slate and start from scratch.
The change flag button lets you \nset the flag for the current vessel.
